answer_1.quote: Fact checking aims to predict the factuality and provide convincing justifications, to evaluate the claim as Factual, Non-Factual, or Not Enough Information, based on a knowledge source as auxiliary information (AI).
answer_1.outputs: The outputs include predicted verdicts (Factual, Non-Factual, Not Enough Information) and generated justifications for fact-checking claims.

answer_2.quote: To audit the fact-checking capacities of LLMs, we introduce three automatic evaluation metrics for quantitative analysis: Insight Mastery Rate (IMR), Justification Flaw Rate (JFR), and Grade.

answer_3.quote: The Evaluator agent scores the target LLM's predicted verdict and generated justification via LLM-as-a-Judge, i.e., F α (x).
methods: scoring prompt with reference answer comparison

answer_4.quote: 3 professional fact-checking annotators (between the ages of 26 and 29) were asked to judge whether the quality of fact-checking data on each sample was up to standard or not
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluated: 1) suitability of taxonomy, 2) check-worthiness of claim, 3) ground truth status of evidence, 4) value of simulated conversation, 5) correctness of reference answer, 6) acceptability of agent score and comment.
